items.title: The inequality [Gamma_B : Gamma_A] times [kappa_B : kappa_A] at most [L : K] for a finite extension of valuation rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement controls a finite extension L over K of fraction fields of valuation rings A contained in B by the two invariants of the extension of valuation rings: it asserts that the residue field extension is finite, that the index of Gamma_A in Gamma_B is finite, and that the product of the two degrees is at most the degree of the field extension (statement lines 37333-37342). The proof is the standard construction of a K-linearly independent family of size equal to the product of the two invariants: units of B that are independent modulo the maximal ideal, and nonzero elements with distinct classes in Gamma_B over Gamma_A, are multiplied together and shown to be linearly independent by a minimal-valuation argument in which the two choices enter at different places (proof lines 37345-37371). The delicate point is that the index set of minimal valuation has to be reduced to a single value of the second index before the residue classes of the first family can be used, which is exactly why the two families are chosen in the way they are. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing, and the remark that follows the lemma at source lines 37330-37331, saying that the field extension is not required to be finite, is outside the counted spans.
